findings.issue: The fallback is correct for persistence and for reservation. The item is stored as PLATFORM, so it is never NULL. Only the reserve StockLine sends sellerId null, and inventory resolves the owner itself or throws OutOfStock, so stock stays fail-closed. However, this re-opens the latent ledger mismatch from security s2r1 minor 1. If inventory resolves a real owner S, it consumes S's stock, while the item, the shipment, seller visibility and the seller-service sale booking all say PLATFORM. The existing test offerWithUnknownSellerIsPlatform now asserts exactly that split: the allocation carries owner, and the item and shipment are PLATFORM. The path is unreachable while product.offers.seller_id is NOT NULL (V7), and base behaved the same way, so this is minor. But stock and order are only consistent when the allocation owner is null or PLATFORM.
findings.fix: Follow-up: the cleaner fail-closed option is security's alternative. Reject an offer line whose owner is unknown at placement (PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE) before save, and drop ownerlessOffers. Otherwise, record the accepted mismatch in design.md or the register, and change the test name and comment so the test does not read as intended behaviour.

findings.issue: The round-2 attach change is now dead code in production. The only caller of addItem is OrderService.draft (OrderService.java:687), and it always passes a non-null sellerId (PLATFORM or offer.sellerId). splitOff copies sellerId. No test calls the 8-arg addItem overload that passes null. So item.getSellerId() is never null in attach, and the al.sellerId() branch never runs. The pre-existing `if (item.getSellerId()==null) item.tagOffer(...)` (lines 804-806) is also dead, and it could never have persisted anyway because seller_id is updatable=false and attach runs after the first save. Leaving it in suggests that the owner from the allocation is honoured, which it is not.
findings.fix: Revert attach to the base expression `item.getSellerId() == null ? PLATFORM_SELLER : item.getSellerId()`. Either delete the post-save tagOffer, or replace it with a comment that seller_id is fixed at insert.

findings.issue: oldAllocationShapeHasNullSellerId autowires the Jackson 2 com.fasterxml ObjectMapper bean. It proves the record annotations and Jackson defaults (it would fail if ignoreUnknown were removed or FAIL_ON_MISSING_CREATOR_PROPERTIES were enabled). It does not prove that the mapper is the one the Feign decoder uses, which on Spring Boot 4 may be Jackson 3.
findings.fix: Optional: decode through the Feign decoder or the HttpMessageConverters the client uses, or note the assumption.

findings.issue: Removing `&& sellerId != null` restores the base behaviour: if an ownerless offer has a sellerName, that name is put under PLATFORM_SELLER, and the platform shipment is labelled with a seller's name. Also, `new java.util.HashSet<>()` is fully qualified while Set is now imported. This is unreachable under V7.
findings.fix: Only put the name when offer.sellerId() != null. Import HashSet.

summary: The regression fix is correct. draft keeps sellerId=PLATFORM for an ownerless offer, so order_items.seller_id is set at insert and never NULL. ownerlessOffers nulls the sellerId only on the reserve StockLine (contains(null) on a HashSet is safe), so inventory resolves the owner or rejects the line, and reservation stays fail-closed. The cost is that an owner resolved by inventory is not reflected on the order. This re-opens the unreachable (V7 NOT NULL) ledger mismatch flagged as security s2r1 minor 1, and a test now asserts it (minor). The round-2 Order.attach change is dead code in production: every item reaches attach with a non-null seller. It should be reverted to the base expression (minor). The tests have teeth. Both placement tests read seller_id from order_items and order_shipments through JdbcTemplate (the class is not @Transactional), so the NULL regression at 4ea8ca92 would fail containsExactly(PLATFORM). The captured StockLine assertion (sellerId null) would catch removal of the fallback. The shipment assertion in the owner-stub test would catch attach preferring al.sellerId over the item's seller. The old-shape test would fail if ignoreUnknown or the creator-default behaviour changed (nit: it uses the Jackson 2 bean). The inventory concurrency bound isBetween(0,5) is sound: seed 10, at least one absolute setStock(5), then only decrements. The tautological hasSize was dropped. No other updatable=false field is mutated after save. Order.switchPaymentMethod, applyMoney, begin and consumeCart all run before store.save. OrderShipment's updatable=false fields are set only in OrderShipment.of at insert. splitOff inserts new rows and only changes the updatable quantity and lineTotal. tagOffer in attach rewrites offerId with the same value. CEO verify at 64fdb21d passed (313 tests, 0 failures). There are no blockers or majors and all ACs are met, so the verdict is approve.
